alex: FYI ran a set of RoPE-scaling runs across NTK/linear/YARN for Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8B and Qwen-7. Need eyes — saw some perplexity cliffs and a KV-cache memory spike on one config.

maria: ok good catch, high level summary?

alex: TL;DR: NTK looks stable for Mistral at modest scaling (~<=1.05). Qwen shows a sharp ppl cliff around 1.06 at long context (>=16k). Mixtral+YARN triggers large KV page growth when kernel falls back to generic path at seq>4k. Latency/throughput tradeoffs vary by forcing kernel vs letting fallback.

raj: can you paste the main numbers (ppl / p95 / tok/s) so we know magnitude?

alex: sure — quick paste from the bench run: 

alex: ```
model       variant  scale  ppl   p95_ms  tok/s
mistral-7b  ntk      1.04   3.6   28      6200
mistral-7b  linear   1.10   3.58  32      5900
qwen-7b     ntk      1.02   4.1   35      5400
qwen-7b     ntk      1.06   6.2   42      4800  # cliff at longctx
mixtral-8b   yarn    1.00   3.9   40      5600
mixtral-8b   yarn    1.08   4.0   65      3500  # kv page blowup
```

maria: the mixtral row is scary — do we have kernel selection traces? which kernel was chosen before fallback?

alex: runtime chose the new v2-opt kernel for YARN normally, but for shard+seq_len>4096 it fell back to aten_generic because v2-opt doesn't cover that seq/stride pattern yet. I pulled traces: 

alex: ```
[TRACE] kernel_select: model=mixtral-8b seq=4096 preferred=v2-opt -> fallback=aten_generic
[TRACE] kv_cache_alloc: new_page_count=18 -> trigger_gc
[TRACE] gc: freed_pages=3 live_pages=15
[WARN] kv_fragmentation: ratio=0.87
```

sam: could our recent change to max_batch_tokens be pushing average batch seq lengths up and causing this? we changed that cap last week.

alex: yes — continuous batching + higher max_batch_tokens increases chances of hitting >4k sequences combined in a batch. That pushes some requests into the fallback kernel path which doesn't pre-allocate kv pages efficiently. I reran with max_batch_tokens cap=12k and saw throughput fall but kv_page_count stabilized.

raj: what's the hypothesis on the Qwen cliff at scale=1.06? seems model-specific.

alex: Qwen's rotary implementation couples head_dim and phase increment; NTK-style scaling changes the cosine decay which effectively changes the phase for high head counts. At long contexts this produces aliasing, amplifying logits and degrading ppl. The linear variant doesn't show the same aliasing but has worse latency due to different matmul kernels.

maria: can we do a controlled matrix of toggles: (A) force kernel=v2-opt, (B) disable continuous batching, (C) apply small prefix cache warmup, (D) clip scale to safe range per model?

alex: ran quick toggles: forcing kernel (A) prevents mixtral kv blowup but p95 goes up ~6ms due to slower codegen path. Disabling continuous batching (B) eliminates Qwen cliff at 1.06 but throughput drops ~8%. Prefix warming (C) helps slightly for mixtral by pre-allocating page slots. Clipping scale (D) is simplest: we can have per-model safe max scale.

bench-bot: perf-run complete: run_id=pr_1748123456_01. Report: https://bench.internal/reports/pr_1748123456

alex: Proposed safe ranges from these runs: Mistral-7B: <=1.08, Qwen-7B: <=1.03 (NTK), Mixtral-8B (YARN): avoid >1.02 unless kernel extension applied. I'll open a runtime PR to add: 1) per-model scale caps, 2) kernel pinning config, 3) telemetry alerts for kv_page_count and kernel_fallback_rate.

maria: please also add an eval job that runs ppl at lengths [2k,4k,8k,16k,32k] for any scale change so we catch cliffs in CI.

alex: yup adding an eval harness and a lightweight rollout gate in the console: if ppl delta > 1.0 at any length, block auto-rollout.

raj: can the runtime auto-select a different batching heuristic when kernel_fallback_rate>threshold? i.e., prefer smaller batches to avoid fallback at cost of slightly more latency.

alex: good idea — implement an adaptive policy: if fallback_rate > 5% and avg_seq_len > 3k, decrease max_batch_tokens and set continuous_batching=false for that model. I'll prototype.

sam: also add a note to the release notes: "kernel fallback can increase KV fragmentation on YARN shards" and include recommended mitigations. :memo:

infra-bot: queued patch: runtime/patches/pr-3212 kernel-pin + telemetry to staging

alex: next steps: (1) finalize PR with per-model safe ranges, (2) add eval harness and CI gate, (3) prototype adaptive batching policy, (4) we need a perf follow-up to extend v2-opt kernels to cover the seq/stride pattern for YARN shards.

maria: thanks — can you dump the small reproducer for mixtral kv blowup into the ticket? one-line run command would be handy.

alex: will attach reproducer and a tiny script that toggles max_batch_tokens and kernel pin.

sam: ack, thanks alex. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy to staging started (job 4598).
